reading.title: Recruitment and Selection Policy: fair selection
paragraphs: 3. SELECTION

3.1 The Company is committed to appointing the best person for each role, on merit alone. Every selection decision must be based on the essential and desirable criteria set out in the person specification, and on nothing else.

3.2 Shortlisting shall be carried out by at least two people, one of whom must be the hiring manager. Each of them shall score the applications independently against the published criteria before comparing notes.

3.3 Interviews shall be structured. All candidates for the same role shall be asked the same core questions, although interviewers may probe further in the light of the answers given. Questions must relate directly to the requirements of the role. Interviewers shall refrain from asking about a candidate's age, family circumstances, health, origins, religious beliefs or trade union membership.
3.4 Where a candidate has made the Company aware of a disability, the interview arrangements shall be adapted as far as is reasonably practicable.
3.5 Candidates must be told in advance of any test or assessment method that will be used. Such methods must be relevant to the role, and the results shall remain confidential.
3.6 References shall be taken up only after a conditional offer has been made, and only with the candidate's knowledge.

3.7 Interview notes and scoring matrices shall be returned to Human Resources within two working days of the final interview. They shall be retained for the period set out in the Company's data retention schedule, so that the Company is able to give feedback on request and, if need be, to account for its decision.
3.8 Unsuccessful candidates shall be informed promptly and courteously. No candidate should learn the outcome from a third party.

reading.title: Invitation to an assessment day
paragraphs: Dear Mr Okafor,
Graduate HR Programme - invitation to assessment day

Thank you for your application and for the time you gave us on the telephone last week. I am delighted to tell you that you have been shortlisted, and we would like to invite you to an assessment day at our Leeds office on Thursday 12 June.

The day will start at 9.15 a.m. and should finish by 4 p.m. It will consist of a group exercise, a short written case study and a competency-based interview with two members of our HR leadership team. You will not need to prepare a presentation, but you may find it helpful to think of examples from your studies, internships or other activities that show how you work with other people.

Please bring your passport or another document proving your right to work in the United Kingdom. We are happy to reimburse reasonable travel expenses against receipts. Lunch will be provided, so do let us know if you have any dietary requirements.

If you have a disability or a health condition and would like us to make adjustments to any part of the day, please tell us as soon as you can; anything you share will be treated in confidence and will play no part in our decision.

I would be grateful if you could confirm your attendance by replying to this email by Friday 6 June. Should the date be impossible for you, please ring me on the number below and we will do our best to find an alternative.
We aim to let all candidates know the outcome within five working days.
We look forward to meeting you.
Yours sincerely,

Hannah Whitfield
Talent Acquisition Partner

reading.title: Hiring your first employee in France: what to do before day one
paragraphs:
To: Sarah Lindqvist, COO, Northlight Analytics Ltd
From: Claire Morel
Re: Your first hire in Lyon - formalities before the start date

You asked me to set out what has to be in place before your new Sales Manager starts on 1 September. In France, taking someone on is not simply a matter of signing a contract: several formalities fall to the employer, and the first of them must be completed before the employee does any work at all.

1. Pre-hiring declaration. You must file a declaration (the 'DPAE') with URSSAF, the body that collects social security contributions, shortly before the start date. It is done online and takes a few minutes. Failing to file it exposes the company to penalties for undeclared work, so please do not let anyone start, even for a handover day, until we have confirmation that it has gone through.
2. Staff register. Every establishment must keep a register listing its employees in order of hiring. The new recruit's details have to be entered on the day he joins.

3. Occupational health. You will need to sign up with an occupational health service, which will arrange an information and prevention appointment for him after he starts. This is not a pre-employment medical, and the offer cannot be made conditional on it.

4. Right to work. Your candidate is a Canadian national. Before he starts, we must check that his residence permit allows him to take up salaried employment and have its authenticity verified by the préfecture. I would allow some time for this, as it cannot be done at the last minute.
None of this is difficult, but the sequence matters. I suggest we deal with points 1 and 4 first; I can handle the filings on your behalf once you have given me a mandate to do so.
Do call me if anything is unclear.

reading.title: Recruitment agency terms of business: fees and rebate
paragraphs: 6. FEES
6.1 In consideration of the Services, the Client shall pay the Agency a fee equal to [twenty] per cent of the Candidate's gross annual basic salary for the first year of the Engagement (the 'Fee').
6.2 The Fee shall become due upon the Candidate's acceptance of an offer of employment from the Client and shall be payable within [thirty] days of the date of the Agency's invoice.

6.3 The Fee shall be payable in respect of any Candidate introduced by the Agency who is engaged by the Client, or by any company in the Client's group, within [twelve] months of the Introduction, whether or not the Agency was involved in the final stages of the selection process.
6.4 For the avoidance of doubt, no fee shall be payable where no Engagement takes place.
7. REBATE

7.1 Should the Engagement terminate for any reason other than redundancy within [twelve] weeks of the start date, the Agency shall, at the Client's option, either seek a replacement Candidate at no additional charge or refund the Fee on the sliding scale set out in Schedule 2.
7.2 The Client shall not be entitled to a rebate unless it has paid the Fee in full by the due date and has notified the Agency in writing within [seven] days of the termination.
8. NON-SOLICITATION

8.1 The Agency undertakes not to approach, directly or indirectly, any Candidate placed with the Client under this Agreement with a view to offering him or her alternative employment, for a period of [twelve] months from the start date.
9. CANDIDATE INFORMATION

9.1 The Agency shall use reasonable endeavours to verify the accuracy of the information supplied by a Candidate. The Client nevertheless remains responsible for taking up references and for satisfying itself that the Candidate is suitable and is entitled to work in the relevant country.

writing.title: Inviting a candidate to interview
writing.brief: You are recruiting an HR Adviser for a client. Write to a shortlisted candidate, Ms Daniels, inviting her to a first interview: date and place, who she will meet, how long it will last, what to bring, and how to confirm.
writing.brief_fr: Vous recrutez un(e) HR Adviser pour un client. Écrivez à une candidate présélectionnée, Mme Daniels, pour l'inviter à un premier entretien : date et lieu, interlocuteurs, durée, documents à apporter et modalités de confirmation.

gaps.text: Thank you for ___ for the position of HR Adviser.
gaps.explain_fr: « To apply for a position » : après « thank you for », le verbe prend -ing. Ni « postulating » ni « candidating ».

gaps.text: We were impressed by your application and would like to ___ you to an interview.
gaps.explain_fr: En anglais, on « invite » un candidat ; « convoke » et « summon » sont à proscrire.

gaps.text: The interview will ___ place at our offices on Tuesday 3 June at 10 a.m.
gaps.explain_fr: « To take place » = avoir lieu. « To have place » est un calque.

gaps.text: You will meet Mark Ellis, the ___ manager, and myself, and the conversation should last about an hour.
gaps.explain_fr: « The hiring manager » = le responsable opérationnel qui recrute pour son équipe.

gaps.text: Please ___ proof of your right to work in the UK with you.
gaps.explain_fr: « To bring » (apporter vers le lieu où se trouve le destinataire), et non « to take » ni « to carry ».

gaps.text: I would be grateful if you could confirm your ___ by Friday.
gaps.explain_fr: « To confirm one's attendance » = confirmer sa présence. « Presence » ne s'emploie pas dans ce contexte.

writing.model:
Subject: Interview - HR Adviser

Dear Ms Daniels,

Thank you for applying for the position of HR Adviser. We were impressed by your application and would like to invite you to an interview.

The interview will take place at our offices on Tuesday 3 June at 10 a.m. You will meet Mark Ellis, the hiring manager, and myself, and the conversation should last about an hour.

Please bring proof of your right to work in the UK with you. I would be grateful if you could confirm your attendance by Friday. If the time doesn't suit you, do let me know and I will try to find an alternative.

We look forward to meeting you.

Kind regards,
Claire Morel
writing.model_us:
Subject: Interview - HR Advisor

Dear Ms. Daniels,

Thank you for applying for the position of HR Advisor. We were impressed by your application and would like to invite you to an interview.

The interview will take place at our offices on Tuesday, June 3, at 10 a.m. You will meet with Mark Ellis, the hiring manager, and me, and the conversation should last about an hour.

Please bring documents showing that you are authorized to work in the United States. I would appreciate it if you could confirm that you can attend by Friday. If the time doesn't work for you, just let me know and I will try to find an alternative.

We look forward to meeting you.

commentary.quote: We were impressed by your application
commentary.note_fr: Un compliment sobre en ouverture donne le ton : le candidat est aussi quelqu'un à convaincre.

commentary.quote: the conversation should last about an hour
commentary.note_fr: « Should » exprime ici une prévision raisonnable, sans engagement ferme. « Conversation » est plus engageant que « interview » répété.

commentary.quote: If the time doesn't suit you, do let me know
commentary.note_fr: « To suit someone » = convenir à quelqu'un (UK) ; un Américain dira « doesn't work for you ». Le « do » d'insistance rend l'invitation chaleureuse.

commentary.quote: We look forward to meeting you.
commentary.note_fr: « To » est une préposition : verbe en -ing obligatoire. Formule de clôture standard avant un rendez-vous.

commentary.quote: Kind regards,
commentary.note_fr: Formule de politesse courante dans un e-mail professionnel britannique ; « Yours sincerely » serait réservé à une lettre.

checklist: Have I named the position in the first sentence?
Are the date, time, place and length of the interview all stated?
Does the candidate know whom she will meet and what to bring?
Have I said how and by when to confirm?
Is the tone warm without being familiar?
phrasebank: Thank you for applying for the position of...
We would like to invite you to an interview.
The interview will take place at... on... at...
You will meet..., the hiring manager.
I would be grateful if you could confirm your attendance by...
If the time doesn't suit you, do let me know.
We look forward to meeting you.

writing.title: Turning down a candidate after interview
writing.brief: After final interviews for a Payroll Manager position, write to Mr Hughes, who came second. Thank him, tell him he has not been selected, give one piece of honest feedback, and ask whether you may keep his details for future vacancies.
writing.brief_fr: À l'issue des entretiens finaux pour un poste de Payroll Manager, écrivez à M. Hughes, arrivé deuxième. Remerciez-le, annoncez-lui qu'il n'est pas retenu, donnez-lui un élément de retour sincère et demandez-lui si vous pouvez conserver son dossier pour de futurs postes.

gaps.text: Thank you for taking the time to ___ us last week.
gaps.explain_fr: « To meet someone » est transitif direct en anglais britannique ; « to meet with » est plutôt américain.

gaps.text: I am ___ to say that we will not be taking your application any further on this occasion.
gaps.explain_fr: « I am sorry to say that » ou « I am afraid that » adoucit l'annonce. Notez « on this occasion », qui laisse la porte ouverte.

gaps.text: The panel was impressed by your technical knowledge; ___, another candidate had more experience of managing a team, which is central to this role.
gaps.explain_fr: « However », après un point-virgule et suivi d'une virgule, introduit la restriction. « But » ne peut pas occuper cette place.

gaps.text: We would be happy to keep your details on ___ for future vacancies.
gaps.explain_fr: « To keep something on file » = conserver au dossier. C'est la formule consacrée pour un vivier de candidats.

gaps.text: With your ___, we would contact you should a suitable role arise; just let me know whether you are comfortable with that.
gaps.explain_fr: Conserver un CV suppose l'accord du candidat : « with your consent ». « Accord » existe en anglais, mais pas dans ce sens.

gaps.text: I wish you every ___ in your search.
gaps.explain_fr: « I wish you every success » : formule de clôture élégante. « Good luck » serait trop familier, « all the success » incorrect.

writing.model:
Subject: Payroll Manager - outcome of your interview

Dear Mr Hughes,

Thank you for taking the time to meet us last week. It was a pleasure to talk to you.

I am sorry to say that we will not be taking your application any further on this occasion. The panel was impressed by your technical knowledge; however, another candidate had more experience of managing a team, which is central to this role. It was a close decision.

We would be happy to keep your details on file for future vacancies. With your consent, we would contact you should a suitable role arise; just let me know whether you are comfortable with that.

I wish you every success in your search.

Kind regards,
Claire Morel

commentary.quote: we will not be taking your application any further on this occasion
commentary.note_fr: La formule évite « rejected » et « refused ». Le futur progressif (« will not be taking ») présente la décision comme un fait, sans brutalité.

commentary.quote: which is central to this role
commentary.note_fr: Le retour porte sur un critère du poste, non sur la personne : c'est ce qui le rend à la fois utile et inattaquable.

commentary.quote: It was a close decision.
commentary.note_fr: Phrase courte, sincère, qui valorise le candidat sans rien promettre. À n'écrire que si c'est vrai.

commentary.quote: should a suitable role arise
commentary.note_fr: Inversion soutenue pour « if a suitable role arises ». « To arise » se dit d'un poste, d'une occasion, d'un problème.

commentary.quote: just let me know whether you are comfortable with that
commentary.note_fr: On demande un accord explicite pour la conservation des données ; « comfortable with » est la tournure naturelle pour « d'accord avec ».

checklist: Have I thanked the candidate before giving the news?
Is the decision stated clearly, in the second paragraph at the latest?
Is my feedback linked to a requirement of the role rather than to the person?
Have I avoided any comment that could suggest a discriminatory reason?
Have I asked for consent before keeping his details?
phrasebank: Thank you for taking the time to meet us.
I am sorry to say that we will not be taking your application any further.
On this occasion, another candidate more closely matched the requirements of the role.
It was a close decision.
We would be happy to keep your details on file.
Should a suitable role arise, we would be in touch.
I wish you every success in your search.

writing.title: Explaining French internships to a British client
writing.brief: A British client wants to take on 'a couple of unpaid interns' in its Paris office to cover for an employee on maternity leave. Write one paragraph of a client note explaining why this is not possible as described and what the rules are.
writing.brief_fr: Un client britannique souhaite prendre « deux ou trois stagiaires non rémunérés » dans son bureau parisien pour remplacer une salariée en congé de maternité. Rédigez un paragraphe de note au client expliquant pourquoi ce n'est pas possible en l'état et quelles sont les règles.
outline: An internship in France requires a three-party agreement with the student's school
The intern is not an employee and must have a learning purpose
An intern cannot replace an absent employee or fill a permanent job
Beyond a minimum length, a monthly allowance is compulsory
The risk, and the alternative: a fixed-term contract
writing.model: Internships are tightly regulated in France, and I am afraid the arrangement you have in mind would not be lawful as it stands. An intern can only be taken on under a three-party agreement signed by the student, his or her school or university and the host company; without an educational institution, there is no internship. The intern is not an employee: the placement must serve a learning purpose linked to the course, and a supervisor has to be appointed within the team. It follows that an intern may not be used to cover for an absent employee or to fill a permanent position, which rules out your maternity cover. Nor can the internship be unpaid if it lasts beyond the minimum period laid down by law, since a monthly allowance then becomes compulsory. The risk is real: a court could treat the relationship as an employment contract, with back pay and social security contributions to match. For the maternity leave, a fixed-term contract is the appropriate tool, and I would be glad to prepare one. If you would also like to welcome a student, we can set up a genuine internship alongside it.

commentary.quote: I am afraid the arrangement you have in mind would not be lawful as it stands
commentary.note_fr: Refus poli et précis : « I am afraid » adoucit, « as it stands » (en l'état) laisse entendre qu'une solution existe.

commentary.quote: without an educational institution, there is no internship
commentary.note_fr: Une phrase brève et symétrique fixe la règle dans l'esprit du lecteur mieux qu'une longue explication.

commentary.quote: which rules out your maternity cover
commentary.note_fr: « To rule out » = exclure. La relative ramène la règle générale au cas concret du client.

commentary.quote: Nor can the internship be unpaid
commentary.note_fr: « Nor » en tête de phrase entraîne l'inversion auxiliaire-sujet : tournure soignée pour ajouter une seconde interdiction.

commentary.quote: with back pay and social security contributions to match
commentary.note_fr: « Back pay » = rappel de salaire ; « to match » = à l'avenant. Le risque est chiffré en nature, sans montant inventé.

commentary.quote: I would be glad to prepare one
commentary.note_fr: Après le refus, une proposition : la note se termine sur ce que le consultant peut faire, pas sur l'interdit.

checklist: Have I said clearly, and politely, that the plan does not work as described?
Is the three-party agreement explained in plain words?
Have I linked each rule to the client's actual plan?
Is the risk stated without inventing figures?
Does the paragraph end with a practical alternative?
phrasebank: I am afraid the arrangement you have in mind would not be lawful as it stands.
An intern can only be taken on under...
It follows that...
..., which rules out...
Nor can...
The risk is real: a court could treat the relationship as...
... is the appropriate tool, and I would be glad to prepare one.

writing.title: Minutes of a selection panel meeting
writing.brief: You took the notes at the panel's meeting after final interviews for a Finance Business Partner. Write the 'Decision' section of the minutes: three candidates (A, B and C), the panel's assessment, the decision, the reserve candidate and the next steps.
writing.brief_fr: Vous avez pris les notes de la réunion du jury à l'issue des entretiens finaux pour un poste de Finance Business Partner. Rédigez la section « Décision » du compte rendu : trois candidats (A, B et C), l'appréciation du jury, la décision, le candidat de réserve et les prochaines étapes.
outline: How the candidates were assessed (scores against the criteria)
Candidate A: strongest overall, one reservation
Candidate B: close second, kept in reserve
Candidate C: did not meet one essential criterion
Decision and next steps, with owners and dates
writing.model:
4. Decision

The panel compared the scores awarded independently by its three members against the six criteria in the person specification. Candidate A obtained the highest overall score and was particularly strong on stakeholder management and commercial awareness. One reservation was noted: she has not yet worked in a listed company. The panel took the view that this could be addressed during induction. Candidate B was a close second, with excellent technical skills but less evidence of influencing senior managers. Candidate C, although an engaging interviewee, did not meet the essential criterion relating to a professional accounting qualification.

It was agreed unanimously to offer the position to Candidate A, subject to satisfactory references, and to hold Candidate B in reserve until the offer has been accepted. No candidate is to be turned down before then.

Actions: JP to telephone Candidate A with a verbal offer by 14 May. CM to take up references once the offer has been accepted in principle. CM to give feedback to Candidate C by 16 May. All panel members to return their scoring matrices to HR by 13 May.

commentary.quote: The panel took the view that
commentary.note_fr: Tournure impersonnelle typique des comptes rendus : on rapporte la position collective, pas les échanges.

commentary.quote: was a close second
commentary.note_fr: « A close second » = deuxième de peu. Formule sobre, utile pour justifier la mise en réserve.

commentary.quote: did not meet the essential criterion relating to
commentary.note_fr: Le motif d'écartement est rattaché à un critère publié : c'est ce qui rend la décision défendable.

commentary.quote: It was agreed unanimously to offer the position to Candidate A, subject to satisfactory references
commentary.note_fr: Passif impersonnel (« It was agreed ») et réserve juridique (« subject to ») : le style même du procès-verbal.

commentary.quote: JP to telephone Candidate A
commentary.note_fr: Dans les actions, on écrit « initiales + to + verbe » : l'infinitif exprime ce qui reste à faire, avec une échéance.

checklist: Have I reported decisions and reasons rather than who said what?
Is each assessment tied to a criterion in the person specification?
Are the candidates anonymised consistently?
Is the decision recorded with its condition (references)?
Does every action have an owner and a date?
phrasebank: The panel compared the scores awarded against the criteria.
One reservation was noted: ...
The panel took the view that...
Candidate B was a close second.
It was agreed unanimously to..., subject to...
... to hold Candidate B in reserve until...
Actions: [initials] to... by [date].

writing.title: A recommendation report on the final candidates
writing.brief: You have run a search for a Head of HR for a British client's French subsidiary. Write the short report that goes with your shortlist of two finalists, Ms Laurent and Mr Bernard: summary of the search, a profile of each, your recommendation and the next steps.
writing.brief_fr: Vous avez mené la recherche d'un(e) Head of HR pour la filiale française d'un client britannique. Rédigez le bref rapport accompagnant votre présélection de deux finalistes, Mme Laurent et M. Bernard : bilan de la recherche, portrait de chacun, recommandation et prochaines étapes.
outline: Purpose of the report and summary of the search (numbers, stages)
Ms Laurent: strengths, one point to explore, availability
Mr Bernard: strengths, one point to explore, availability
Recommendation, with reasons tied to the brief
Proposed next steps and timetable
writing.model:
Head of HR, France - shortlist report

1. Purpose
This report presents the two candidates we recommend for final interview and sets out our assessment of each against the brief agreed in March.

2. The search
We approached forty-two people, most of whom were not actively looking, and received eighteen applications in response to the advertisement. Eleven candidates were interviewed by telephone and five in person. Two stand out.

3. Ms Laurent
Ms Laurent has led the HR function of a 400-strong industrial site for six years. She has a strong track record in dealing with employee representatives and negotiated two company-level agreements last year. Her English is fluent. The point to explore at interview is her limited exposure to a matrix organisation. She is on three months' notice.

4. Mr Bernard
Mr Bernard is currently HR Business Partner in a listed services group and is used to reporting to a head office abroad. He is an excellent communicator and would get up to speed quickly on your systems. He has, however, less first-hand experience of collective bargaining, which the brief treats as essential. He could start within six weeks.

5. Recommendation
Both candidates meet the essential criteria. On balance, we would put Ms Laurent slightly ahead, given the negotiations planned for next year. Mr Bernard would nevertheless be a very credible choice, particularly if an early start is your priority.

6. Next steps
We suggest that both candidates meet your Managing Director in Paris in the week of 16 June. With your agreement, we would then take up references on the preferred candidate before any offer is made.

commentary.quote: most of whom were not actively looking
commentary.note_fr: Relative avec quantifieur (« most of whom ») : très utile, et impossible à calquer du français. « Not actively looking » = candidats passifs.

commentary.quote: Two stand out.
commentary.note_fr: Une phrase de trois mots après une série de chiffres : le changement de rythme met la conclusion en valeur.

commentary.quote: The point to explore at interview is
commentary.note_fr: Plutôt que « weakness », on nomme « a point to explore » : factuel, et tourné vers l'action du client.

commentary.quote: which the brief treats as essential
commentary.note_fr: La réserve est rattachée au cahier des charges convenu avec le client, non à une impression.

commentary.quote: On balance, we would put Ms Laurent slightly ahead
commentary.note_fr: « On balance » (tout bien pesé) et « slightly » : une recommandation nette, formulée avec la retenue britannique.

commentary.quote: With your agreement, we would then take up references
commentary.note_fr: « To take up references » (UK). Le conditionnel et « with your agreement » laissent la décision au client.

checklist: Does the opening say what the report is for?
Are the two profiles built in the same way, so that they can be compared?
Is every judgement linked to the brief or to evidence?
Is my recommendation clear but appropriately cautious?
Have I avoided any reference to age, family or other personal characteristics?
Do the next steps include dates?
phrasebank: This report presents... and sets out our assessment of each against the brief.
We approached... people, most of whom...
She has a strong track record in...
The point to explore at interview is...
Both candidates meet the essential criteria.
On balance, we would put... slightly ahead, given...
With your agreement, we would then...

writing.title: A welcome email before the first day
writing.brief: A new HR Coordinator, Tom Reilly, starts on Monday 1 September. Write the email he receives the week before: welcome, arrangements for the first morning, documents to bring, what the first week looks like, his buddy, and whom to contact.
writing.brief_fr: Un nouveau HR Coordinator, Tom Reilly, arrive le lundi 1er septembre. Rédigez l'e-mail qu'il reçoit la semaine précédente : mot de bienvenue, organisation de la première matinée, documents à apporter, déroulement de la première semaine, son parrain d'intégration et la personne à contacter.
outline: Welcome and purpose of the email
First morning: time, place, who will meet him
Documents to bring
Outline of the first week (induction, meetings, equipment)
His buddy; contact before Monday; warm close
writing.model:
Subject: Your first day on Monday 1 September

Dear Tom,

We are all looking forward to welcoming you next week, and I wanted to let you know what to expect.

Please come to reception at 9.30 a.m. on Monday; there is no need to be earlier on your first day. I will meet you there and show you round before introducing you to the team.

Could you bring your passport or identity card, your bank details and your social security number? We need them to finalise your registration, which has to be completed for every new starter.

Your first week is deliberately light. Monday and Tuesday are set aside for your induction, including a health and safety briefing and a session on our HR systems. Your laptop and access rights will be ready when you arrive. From Wednesday you will sit in on a few meetings and spend time with each member of the team, so that you can get up to speed at your own pace.

Sophie Martin, who joined us two years ago, will be your buddy for the first three months. Do ask her anything, however small; she remembers what it is like to be new.

If you have any questions before Monday, just give me a ring on 01 23 45 67 89.

See you next week.

Best wishes,
Claire
writing.model_us:
Subject: Your first day on Monday, September 1

Hi Tom,

We are all looking forward to welcoming you next week, and I wanted to let you know what to expect.

Please come to the front desk at 9:30 a.m. on Monday; there is no need to be earlier on your first day. I will meet you there and show you around before introducing you to the team.

Could you bring your passport or ID card, your bank details, and your social security number? We need them to finalize your registration, which has to be completed for every new hire.

Your first week is deliberately light. Monday and Tuesday are set aside for your orientation, including a health and safety briefing and a session on our HR systems. Your laptop and access rights will be ready when you arrive. Starting Wednesday, you will sit in on a few meetings and spend time with each member of the team, so that you can get up to speed at your own pace.

Sophie Martin, who joined us two years ago, will be your buddy for the first three months. Feel free to ask her anything, however small; she remembers what it is like to be new.

If you have any questions before Monday, just give me a call at 01 23 45 67 89.

See you next week.

Best,
Claire

commentary.quote: I wanted to let you know what to expect
commentary.note_fr: Le prétérit « I wanted » est un adoucisseur courant, plus naturel que « I am writing to inform you » entre futurs collègues.

commentary.quote: show you round
commentary.note_fr: « To show someone round » (UK) / « around » (US) = faire visiter les lieux. Verbe à particule typique de l'accueil.

commentary.quote: Your first week is deliberately light.
commentary.note_fr: Phrase courte qui rassure. « Deliberately » montre que l'intégration est pensée, pas improvisée.

commentary.quote: are set aside for your induction
commentary.note_fr: « To set aside » = réserver (du temps). « Induction » est britannique ; la version américaine dit « orientation ».

commentary.quote: Do ask her anything, however small
commentary.note_fr: Le « do » d'insistance encourage sans familiarité excessive ; « however small » = si minime soit-elle.

commentary.quote: just give me a ring on
commentary.note_fr: « To give someone a ring on » un numéro (UK) ; aux États-Unis : « give me a call at ».

checklist: Does the email sound like a person, not a form?
Are the time and place of arrival unambiguous?
Is the list of documents complete and justified?
Does the new starter know what the first week holds?
Have I named a buddy and a contact?
Is the register friendly but still professional?
phrasebank: We are all looking forward to welcoming you next week.
I wanted to let you know what to expect.
Please come to reception at... on...
I will meet you there and show you round.
Monday and Tuesday are set aside for your induction.
... will be your buddy for the first three months.
If you have any questions before Monday, just give me a ring.
See you next week.

dialogues.title: Taking the brief from a hiring manager
dialogues.context: Claire, an HR consultant, meets Oliver, Head of Operations at a logistics company in Birmingham, to take the brief for a new Site HR Manager.
dialogues.context_fr: Claire, consultante RH, rencontre Oliver, directeur des opérations d'une société de logistique à Birmingham, pour recueillir le besoin concernant un poste de Site HR Manager.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Thanks for making the time, Oliver. Before I draft anything, could you talk me through why the role has come up?
lines.note_fr: « To talk someone through something » = expliquer pas à pas. « To come up » se dit d'un poste qui se libère ou se crée.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Of course. It's a backfill, really. Sandra's moving to head office in September, and frankly I'd like someone in before she goes.
lines.note_fr: « A backfill » = un remplacement, par opposition à une création de poste. « Someone in » : sous-entendu « in post ».

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: That's tight, but not impossible. Is there an up-to-date job description, or are we starting from scratch?
lines.note_fr: « That's tight » : litote britannique pour un délai très court. « From scratch » = de zéro.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: There's one from 2019. I wouldn't trust it. The job's changed a lot since we went to three shifts.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Then let's rewrite it. What would you say are the two or three things this person absolutely must have?
lines.note_fr: Question clé pour distinguer les critères « essential » des « desirable ».

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Someone who can hold their own with the union reps, for a start. And they need to be on the shop floor, not hiding in an office.
lines.note_fr: « To hold one's own » = tenir tête, ne pas se laisser impressionner. « The shop floor » = l'atelier, le terrain.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: So solid employee relations experience in an operational setting. Is a professional HR qualification essential, or just nice to have?
lines.note_fr: Claire reformule la demande familière en critère de sélection. « Nice to have » = souhaitable, non indispensable.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Nice to have. I'd rather have the right person than the right certificate.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Fair enough. And the salary - what have you got approval for?
lines.note_fr: « To have approval for » = disposer d'un budget validé.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Up to fifty-five, but I'd rather not put that in the advert.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I'd gently push back on that. Adverts with a salary range tend to attract far more applicants, and it saves everyone's time.
lines.note_fr: « I'd gently push back on that » : désaccord courtois et assumé. « To push back » = exprimer une réserve.

lines.speaker: Oliver
lines.text: Hmm. Go on, then - put a range in. When could I see a shortlist?
lines.note_fr: « Go on, then » : accord donné à contrecœur, typiquement britannique.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: If we advertise this week and I approach a few people directly, I'd hope to have four or five candidates for you by mid-July.
lines.note_fr: « I'd hope to » : engagement prudent. « To approach someone directly » = approche directe.

questions.q: Why is the company recruiting?
options: The site is opening a third shift
The current HR manager is moving to another job in the company
The current HR manager has resigned
A new role has been created
questions.explain_fr: « It's a backfill » : Sandra rejoint le siège en septembre, il s'agit donc d'un remplacement.

questions.q: What does Oliver consider essential?
options: A professional HR qualification
Experience of working at head office
The ability to deal firmly with union representatives
Fluency in French
questions.explain_fr: « Someone who can hold their own with the union reps » ; le diplôme n'est que « nice to have ».

questions.q: What does Claire persuade Oliver to do?
options: Publish a salary range in the advert
Raise the salary to fifty-five thousand
Postpone Sandra's move
Use a headhunter
questions.explain_fr: Elle « pushes back » sur le refus d'afficher le salaire, et Oliver cède : « put a range in ».

dialogues.title: The wash-up after final interviews
dialogues.context: After a morning of panel interviews for a Learning and Development Manager, Claire reviews the three candidates with Priya, the HR Director, and Daniel, the hiring manager.
dialogues.context_fr: Après une matinée d'entretiens devant jury pour un poste de Learning and Development Manager, Claire fait le point sur les trois candidats avec Priya, DRH, et Daniel, le manager recruteur.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Right, shall we do the wash-up while it's all fresh? Has everyone finished their score sheets?
lines.note_fr: « The wash-up » (UK, familier) = le débriefing à chaud. « Score sheet » = grille de notation individuelle.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Just about. I have to say, I really warmed to James. He'd fit in with the team straight away.
lines.note_fr: « To warm to someone » = éprouver de la sympathie pour quelqu'un. « Straight away » (UK) = tout de suite.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: He was very likeable, I agree. Can I ask what you scored him on programme design, though?
lines.note_fr: Claire ramène la discussion aux critères, sans contredire. « Though » en fin de phrase = cependant.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Ah. A two, to be honest. He was a bit vague when we pressed him.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: I had the same. Lots of 'we', not much 'I'. I couldn't work out what he'd actually done himself.
lines.note_fr: Remarque classique en entretien comportemental : le candidat se cache derrière le « nous ». « To work out » = parvenir à comprendre.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Whereas Amara gave us two very concrete examples, with numbers. I've got her top on four of the six criteria.
lines.note_fr: « Whereas » oppose deux éléments. « I've got her top on » = je la classe première sur.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: She was impressive, no question. I just wondered whether she might be a bit... serious for us?
lines.note_fr: « No question » = sans conteste. L'hésitation annonce un jugement subjectif.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I'd be careful there. 'Serious' isn't on the person specification, and I wouldn't want to have to defend it if she asked for feedback.
lines.note_fr: « I'd be careful there » : mise en garde feutrée. On ne peut écarter un candidat sur un critère absent du profil.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Claire's right. On the evidence, it's Amara. Daniel, could you live with that?
lines.note_fr: « On the evidence » = au vu des éléments. « Could you live with that? » = cela vous irait-il ?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I could. She's clearly the strongest. I suppose I was thinking about Friday drinks rather than the job.
lines.note_fr: Autodérision britannique : il reconnaît son biais avec humour.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Happens to all of us. And the third candidate?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Good, but short on budget experience. I'd keep James as our reserve and let the third one know once Amara has accepted.
lines.note_fr: « Short on » = un peu juste en. « Reserve » = candidat de réserve ; on attend l'acceptation avant d'envoyer les refus.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Agreed. I'll ring Amara this afternoon.
lines.note_fr: « To ring » (UK) = téléphoner à ; aux États-Unis : « to call ».

questions.q: Why does Daniel first prefer James?
options: He gave the best examples
He has the most budget experience
He scored highest on programme design
He found him likeable and a natural fit for the team
questions.explain_fr: « I really warmed to James. He'd fit in with the team » : une préférence de sympathie, non fondée sur les critères.

questions.q: What was the problem with James's answers?
options: He was too serious
It was unclear what he had done personally
He had no relevant experience
He criticised his former employer
questions.explain_fr: « Lots of 'we', not much 'I' » : impossible de savoir ce qu'il avait fait lui-même.

questions.q: Why does Claire object to the word 'serious'?
options: It is not a criterion in the person specification
It is rude
Amara was in fact very funny
Priya had already decided
questions.explain_fr: Un motif absent du profil recherché ne pourrait pas être défendu si la candidate demandait un retour.

dialogues.title: A phone screen
dialogues.context: Megan, a recruiter at a software company in Austin, calls Luis, who has applied for a People Operations Specialist position.
dialogues.context_fr: Megan, recruteuse dans une société de logiciels à Austin, appelle Luis, qui a postulé à un poste de People Operations Specialist.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: Hi Luis, this is Megan from Brightline. Is now still a good time?
lines.note_fr: « Is now still a good time? » : vérification d'usage en début d'appel.

lines.speaker: Luis
lines.text: Hi Megan. Yes, absolutely. Thanks for reaching out.
lines.note_fr: « To reach out » (surtout US) = prendre contact.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: Great. So this is just a quick phone screen, twenty minutes or so. I'll tell you a little about the role, ask you a few questions, and leave time for yours. Sound good?
lines.note_fr: Megan annonce le déroulé : c'est la norme. « Sound good? » = « Does that sound good? », ellipse courante à l'oral.

lines.speaker: Luis
lines.text: Sounds great.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: I see you've been at Corvo for about three years. What's prompting you to look right now?
lines.note_fr: « What's prompting you to look? » : manière neutre de demander les raisons du départ.

lines.speaker: Luis
lines.text: I've learned a lot there, but the team is small and there's not much room to grow. I'm looking for a bigger scope, especially on the systems side.
lines.note_fr: Bonne réponse : positive sur l'employeur actuel, tournée vers l'avenir. « Room to grow » = perspectives d'évolution.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: That makes sense. This role owns onboarding end to end, so there'd be plenty of that. Have you worked with an applicant tracking system?
lines.note_fr: « To own » un processus = en être responsable. « End to end » = de bout en bout.

lines.speaker: Luis
lines.text: Yes, I was the admin for ours. I also rebuilt our new hire orientation last year, which cut the paperwork on day one in half.
lines.note_fr: « New hire orientation » (US) = « induction » (UK). Un résultat chiffré vaut mieux qu'un adjectif.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: Nice. Two practical questions. First, are you authorized to work in the U.S., and would you need sponsorship now or in the future?
lines.note_fr: Question standard et licite aux États-Unis ; on ne demande ni la nationalité ni le lieu de naissance.

lines.speaker: Luis
lines.text: I'm a permanent resident, so no sponsorship needed.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: Perfect. And what are you looking for in terms of compensation?
lines.note_fr: On demande les attentes, pas le salaire actuel : dans de nombreux États, interroger sur l'historique salarial est interdit.

lines.speaker: Luis
lines.text: Based on what I've seen for similar roles, somewhere in the mid-seventies. But I'd want to understand the whole package.
lines.note_fr: « The mid-seventies » = environ 75 000 dollars. Luis donne une fourchette et garde une marge de négociation.

lines.speaker: Megan
lines.text: That's within our range. I'd like to move you forward to an interview with the hiring manager. I'll send over some times this afternoon.
lines.note_fr: « To move someone forward » = faire passer à l'étape suivante. « To send over » = envoyer.

questions.q: Why does Luis want to leave his current job?
options: He was laid off
He wants more scope and room to grow
He dislikes his manager
He wants to work remotely
questions.explain_fr: « The team is small and there's not much room to grow. I'm looking for a bigger scope. »

questions.q: What does Megan ask about Luis's immigration status?
options: His country of birth
His nationality
Whether he is authorized to work and needs sponsorship
When his visa expires
questions.explain_fr: Elle demande seulement s'il est autorisé à travailler et s'il aura besoin d'un « sponsorship ».

questions.q: How does the call end?
options: Megan will set up an interview with the hiring manager
Megan makes him an offer
Luis withdraws his application
Megan says the salary is too high
questions.explain_fr: « I'd like to move you forward to an interview with the hiring manager. »

dialogues.title: An intern by Monday?
dialogues.context: Brad, VP of Marketing at a US company, calls Claire, the French HR consultant who looks after the Paris office. His niece's friend is in Paris and he wants her to start as an intern right away.
dialogues.context_fr: Brad, vice-président marketing d'une société américaine, appelle Claire, la consultante RH française qui suit le bureau de Paris. Une amie de sa nièce est à Paris et il voudrait qu'elle commence un stage immédiatement.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Claire, quick one. I've got a great kid in Paris, Emma, just finished her junior year. Can we get her started as an intern on Monday?
lines.note_fr: « Quick one » = une question rapide. « Junior year » = troisième année d'université américaine.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I'd love to help, Brad, but Monday isn't going to happen. In France you can't bring in an intern without an agreement signed with her school.
lines.note_fr: « Isn't going to happen » : refus direct, à l'américaine, adouci par « I'd love to help ».

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Her school? She's on summer break. It's just a few weeks of helping out with the campaign.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I know it sounds like red tape. But here an internship has to be part of a course of study. No school, no internship. That's the rule.
lines.note_fr: « Red tape » = la paperasserie administrative. La formule « No school, no internship » résume la règle.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Okay. And if her college signs whatever you need?
lines.note_fr: « College » (US) = université.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Then we're in business. It's a three-way agreement: Emma, her college, and us. We also need to name someone on the team as her supervisor.
lines.note_fr: « We're in business » = c'est faisable, on peut y aller.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Fine, I'll supervise her myself. It's unpaid, by the way. She just wants the experience.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: That depends on how long she stays. Past a certain length, we have to pay her a monthly stipend. It's not a salary, but it's not optional either.
lines.note_fr: « Stipend » (US) rend bien la gratification. « Past a certain length » : Claire reste générale plutôt que de citer un seuil de mémoire.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Got it. What if we skip all that and just call her a volunteer?
lines.note_fr: « To skip » = faire l'impasse sur.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: I really wouldn't. If she's doing actual work for the business, a court can treat her as an employee, and then we're looking at undeclared work.
lines.note_fr: « I really wouldn't » : mise en garde ferme en trois mots. « We're looking at » = nous risquons.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Wow. Okay, I don't want that on my desk. What do you need from me?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.text: Just her college's contact details and her dates. I'll send them our template today and, with luck, she could start the week after next.
lines.note_fr: « The week after next » = dans deux semaines. « Template » = modèle de document.

lines.speaker: Brad
lines.text: Perfect. Thanks for keeping me out of trouble.
lines.note_fr: « To keep someone out of trouble » = éviter des ennuis à quelqu'un.

questions.q: Why can't Emma start on Monday?
options: She has no work permit
Brad has no budget
There is no agreement signed with her school yet
The Paris office is closed in summer
questions.explain_fr: En France, un stage suppose une convention tripartite signée avec l'établissement d'enseignement.

questions.q: What does Claire say about paying Emma?
options: Interns are never paid in France
She must receive the minimum wage from day one
It is up to Brad
A monthly stipend becomes compulsory beyond a certain length
questions.explain_fr: « Past a certain length, we have to pay her a monthly stipend » : la gratification devient obligatoire au-delà d'une durée minimale.

questions.q: What is the risk of calling Emma a 'volunteer'?
options: She could be treated as an employee and the work as undeclared
She would lose her student status
Her college would refuse to sign
The company would have to sponsor her visa
questions.explain_fr: Si elle effectue un vrai travail, un juge peut y voir un contrat de travail, avec un risque de travail dissimulé.

roleplays.title: Making a verbal offer
roleplays.situation: You are calling Amara Okoye, the preferred candidate for a Learning and Development Manager position at your client's Paris office, to make her a verbal offer: 62,000 euros, starting 1 September. She is pleased but wants to negotiate.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous appelez Amara Okoye, la candidate retenue pour un poste de Learning and Development Manager au bureau parisien de votre client, pour lui faire une offre orale : 62 000 euros, prise de poste le 1er septembre. Elle est ravie mais souhaite négocier.

turns.model: Hello Amara, it's Claire Morel. I have some good news: the panel was very impressed, and we'd like to offer you the position. Is this a good moment to run through the main terms?
turns.tips_fr: Annoncez la bonne nouvelle tout de suite, puis demandez si le moment convient. « To run through » = passer en revue.

turns.say: That's wonderful, thank you! Yes, please go ahead.
turns.model: The offer is a permanent contract as Learning and Development Manager, at a basic salary of 62,000 euros a year, with a start date of 1 September. It's subject to satisfactory references, and I'll confirm everything in writing by tomorrow.
turns.tips_fr: Trois éléments, dans l'ordre : contrat, salaire, date. N'oubliez pas la réserve « subject to satisfactory references ».

turns.say: Thank you. I'll be honest: I was hoping for something closer to 68. Is there any flexibility?
turns.model: I appreciate your being direct. I can't promise anything on the spot, but I do know how keen they are to have you. Let me take it back to the client and see what room there is. Is the salary the only sticking point?
turns.tips_fr: Ne cédez ni ne refusez à chaud. « Let me take it back to the client » fait gagner du temps ; « sticking point » = point de blocage.

turns.say: Mostly, yes. Though I'm on three months' notice, so 1 September might be difficult.
turns.model: That's helpful to know. I think they'd rather wait for the right person than rush, so I'm fairly confident the date can move. I'll raise both points and get back to you by Thursday at the latest.
turns.tips_fr: Rassurez sur ce qui est négociable et engagez-vous sur un délai précis : « I'll get back to you by Thursday ».

turns.say: That sounds fair. Should I wait before saying anything to my employer?
turns.model: Yes, I'd hold off until you have the written offer and you're happy with it. Please don't resign on the strength of a phone call. I'll be in touch on Thursday, and congratulations again.
turns.tips_fr: Conseil essentiel : ne pas démissionner sur une simple offre orale. « On the strength of » = sur la seule foi de.

roleplays.title: Giving feedback to an unsuccessful candidate
roleplays.situation: James Carter, who was interviewed for a Learning and Development Manager position and not selected, calls you to ask for feedback. He is disappointed and a little defensive. Be honest, specific and kind.
roleplays.situation_fr: James Carter, reçu en entretien pour un poste de Learning and Development Manager et non retenu, vous appelle pour avoir un retour. Il est déçu et un peu sur la défensive. Soyez sincère, précis et bienveillant.

turns.say: Hi Claire, it's James Carter. I got your email. I'm disappointed, obviously, and I'd like to understand what went wrong.
turns.model: Hello James, and thank you for calling. I understand your disappointment, and I'm happy to give you some feedback. First of all, nothing went wrong as such: you interviewed well, and it was a close decision.
turns.tips_fr: Accueillez la déception avant d'expliquer. « As such » (à proprement parler) nuance sans nier.

turns.say: So why didn't I get it? I thought the interview went really well.
turns.model: It did, in many ways. The panel liked your energy and the way you'd fit in with the team. Where the other candidate was stronger was on programme design: her examples were more detailed, with clear results.
turns.tips_fr: Commencez par un point positif réel, puis nommez le critère décisif. Comparez sur un critère, jamais sur la personne.

turns.say: I've designed plenty of programmes. I told you about the leadership academy.
turns.model: You did, and it's clearly a strong project. The difficulty was that you described what the team did, and the panel couldn't quite see your own contribution. Next time, I'd spell out exactly what you decided and delivered yourself.
turns.tips_fr: Reconnaissez le fait, puis formulez un conseil concret. « To spell out » = expliciter.

turns.say: Right. That's fair, I suppose. Is it worth my applying again in the future?
turns.model: Absolutely. With your agreement, I'd like to keep your details on file, because I can think of roles where you'd be a very good fit. And if it would help, I'm happy to send you a couple of lines summarising this feedback.
turns.tips_fr: Terminez sur une ouverture sincère et demandez l'accord pour conserver son dossier : « with your agreement ».

roleplays.title: Hiring a non-EU national in France
roleplays.situation: Rachel, HR Director of a British company, wants its small French subsidiary to hire Arjun, an Indian engineer who has just finished a master's degree in Lyon. She wants him to start next Monday. Explain what has to be done first.
roleplays.situation_fr: Rachel, DRH d'une société britannique, souhaite que sa petite filiale française embauche Arjun, un ingénieur indien qui vient de terminer un master à Lyon. Elle voudrait qu'il commence lundi prochain. Expliquez-lui ce qu'il faut faire au préalable.

turns.say: We've found a brilliant engineer, Arjun, and he's free straight away. Can we get him started on Monday?
turns.model: That's good news, and I'd like to make it happen quickly. But I'm afraid Monday is too soon. Arjun isn't an EU national, so before he starts we have to check what his residence permit allows him to do.
turns.tips_fr: Positif d'abord, puis l'obstacle : « I'm afraid Monday is too soon ». Donnez la raison en une phrase.

turns.say: He's been living in France for two years as a student. Surely he already has the right to work?
turns.model: Not necessarily on a full-time basis. A student permit only allows a limited amount of work. To take a permanent job he'll need a status that authorises employment, and we'll have to see which route applies to someone who has just graduated in France.
turns.tips_fr: « Not necessarily » corrige sans brusquer. Restez général : vous n'êtes pas tenu de citer le nom exact du titre de mémoire.

turns.say: And who sorts that out - him or us?
turns.model: Both, in practice. He applies for the change of status, and we support the application as his employer. We also have to have his document checked by the préfecture before the contract starts. I'd allow several weeks rather than several days.
turns.tips_fr: Répartissez clairement les rôles. « I'd allow several weeks » = prévoyez plusieurs semaines : estimation prudente, sans chiffre inventé.

turns.say: What if we just let him start and tidy up the paperwork afterwards?
turns.model: I'd strongly advise against it. Employing a foreign national without the right authorisation is a criminal offence in France, and it would put Arjun's status at risk too. It's simply not worth it for the sake of a few weeks.
turns.tips_fr: « I'd strongly advise against it » : la formule du conseil ferme. Mentionnez le risque pour l'entreprise et pour le salarié.

turns.say: Understood. So what can we do in the meantime?
turns.model: Quite a lot. We can make him a written offer conditional on his obtaining the right to work, so he knows we're committed. I'll check his current permit this week, and once the authorisation is through I'll file the pre-hiring declaration so he can start the next day.
turns.tips_fr: Finissez sur un plan d'action en trois temps. « Conditional on his obtaining » : gérondif avec possessif, tournure soignée.

roleplays.title: Steering a manager away from risky interview questions
roleplays.situation: You are preparing final interviews with Greg, a sales director at a US client with a team in France. He tells you what he plans to ask a female candidate in her early thirties. Steer him towards lawful, job-related questions without lecturing him.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous préparez les entretiens finaux avec Greg, directeur commercial d'un client américain disposant d'une équipe en France. Il vous indique ce qu'il compte demander à une candidate d'une trentaine d'années. Orientez-le vers des questions licites, en lien avec le poste, sans lui faire la leçon.

turns.say: This job is sixty percent travel. So I'm going to ask her straight out whether she has kids or plans to have any. I need to know.
turns.model: I understand what you're trying to find out, and it's a legitimate concern. But that question would land us in trouble, in France and at home. What you really need to know is whether she can travel, so let's ask her exactly that.
turns.tips_fr: Validez le besoin, écartez la question, proposez l'alternative. « To land someone in trouble » = attirer des ennuis.

turns.say: Okay, but how do I ask that without it sounding like the same thing?
turns.model: Describe the reality of the job and ask everyone the same question. Something like: 'This role involves being away two or three nights most weeks. Is that something you can commit to?' It's about the job, not her private life.
turns.tips_fr: Donnez-lui la phrase toute faite : c'est le plus utile. Insistez sur « ask everyone the same question ».

turns.say: Fine. And she's got a two-year gap on her résumé. Can I at least ask about that?
turns.model: Yes, you can ask what she did during that time, in a neutral way. If she says it was for family reasons, just note it and move on. Don't dig any further, and don't let it weigh in your scoring.
turns.tips_fr: « In a neutral way », « move on », « don't dig » : trois consignes courtes et concrètes.

turns.say: Honestly, this feels like walking on eggshells. Back home I'd just go with my gut.
turns.model: I know it feels restrictive. But a structured interview actually gives you better information than a gut feeling, and it protects you if a candidate ever challenges the decision. Let's take ten minutes now to write five solid questions together.
turns.tips_fr: Répondez à l'agacement par un bénéfice concret. « To go with one's gut » = se fier à son instinct ; « to walk on eggshells » = marcher sur des œufs.

functional.function: Opening an interview and putting the candidate at ease
functional.function_fr: Ouvrir un entretien et mettre le candidat à l'aise

phrases.text: Thank you for coming in today. Did you find us all right?
Thanks for making the time. Can I get you some water before we start?
Let me begin by introducing the members of the panel.
We've got about forty-five minutes. I'll start with a few questions, and there'll be time for yours at the end.
Feel free to take a moment to think before you answer.
We'll both be taking notes, so please don't be put off by that.
So, to kick things off, why don't you walk me through your background?
Perhaps you could start by telling us what attracted you to this role.
Could you give me a specific example of that?
Tell me about a time when you had to deal with a difficult manager.
What exactly was your own role in that project?
And what was the outcome?
With hindsight, is there anything you would have done differently?
Could I take you back to something you said earlier?
Help me understand what that looked like day to day.
You said 'we' - which part of it was down to you?

functional.function_fr: Annoncer le résultat à un candidat

phrases.text: I'm delighted to say that we'd like to offer you the position.
Good news - we'd love to have you on board.
We'd like to take your application forward to the next stage.
We'd like to move you forward to a final interview.
I'm afraid it isn't the news you were hoping for.
I regret to inform you that your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion.
It was a very close decision, and I'd be glad to give you some feedback.
We've decided to go with another candidate, but I'd like to stay in touch.
